Brass is ideal for cases. Malleable enough to hold the crimp, but release the bullet when fired... can also be chamber formed. Corrosion resistant (why they use brass fittings on ships) so can last a long time without compromising the powder. Can also be re-used/loaded. Other metals have been tried. The most popular is steel cased, but the first ones corroded to easy, so they lacquered them, and later polymer coated them. But the lacquer and polymer would melt off or flake in the action of the gun and gum it up causing jams. Several have tried caseless ammo, but they have problems with firing on their own when they come in contact with a hot chamber.... with a few even causing the entire magazine to discharge if the gun got too hot. All plastic/polymer have had strength problems, brittleness, U.V. resistance issues, heat deformation issues, etc. Maybe one day the tech will get there, but today is not that day.
